name: vawe
description: Deterministic motion-graphics engine: one self-describing JSON in, one video out. Renders frame-by-frame in Chrome, encodes with ffmpeg.
//: Rendering is the Go service: `make render M=<format>` / `make all` (see Makefile).
//puppeteer-note: REPO-DEV ONLY, and it must stay here. Its postinstall downloads a full Chrome UNCONDITIONALLY: measured 473MB and 29s on a fast connection, minutes on a normal one, against a 16.3MB package. It used to sit in `dependencies`, so every `npm i vawe` paid that. Nothing the package SHIPS needs it: the browser is launched by chromedp from the Go side (internal/scene/scene.go), which finds a system Chrome on its own, and cli/vawe.mjs only ever asked puppeteer for a PATH STRING it never launched. The 41 repo tools that do need it (gates, beats, reveal) run from a checkout, where devDependencies are installed. optionalDependencies would NOT have fixed this - npm installs those by default too, so the download would still happen.
//oxlint-note: Code-quality enforcement: complexity, function length, nesting depth. Rust, so a whole-repo sweep runs in under a second and a single-file check is instant. That speed is what lets it run on every file WRITE (harness/live/code-quality.mjs) rather than only at push, which is the difference between a rule that shapes code and a rule that scolds after the fact. A comment key must stay at the ROOT of this file: npm parses every key inside devDependencies as a package name, and a `//name` entry there breaks `npm install` outright.
